harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured daily log rotation for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1 (Alpine Linux) using logrotate, keeping 7 compressed rotations with copytruncate so the writer never has to reopen the file. Installed logrotate via apk, wrote /etc/logrotate.d/inventory, enabled/started crond (which runs /etc/periodic/daily/logrotate) so rotation actually fires daily, and validated behavior with forced rotation cycles. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured a pre-restart boot_id baseline, issued a native reboot, polled until node1 was reachable again, confirmed a changed boot_id/uptime, and re-verified crond, the logrotate config, retained rotated files, and continued writability of app.log post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (Alpine 3.23), existing /var/log/inventory/app.log, and cron/logrotate tooling state
apk update && apk add --no-cache logrotate (installs /etc/periodic/daily/logrotate periodic job)
Wrote /etc/logrotate.d/inventory: daily, rotate 7, compress, delaycompress, missingok, notifempty, copytruncate
rc-update add crond default; rc-service crond start (crond was previously stopped and not enabled)
Dry-run validated config with logrotate -d /etc/logrotate.conf
Forced multiple logrotate cycles to prove rotation, compression (delaycompress), retention cap at 7 rotations, and that app.log stays writable (copytruncate) with no service restart needed
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, crond status, config contents, rotation files, live write to app.log
Triggered native reboot on node1 via backgrounded 'sleep 2; reboot' so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again
Verified boot_id changed and uptime shows a fresh boot time, proving an actual restart occurred
Post-restart: verified crond auto-started and is enabled in default runlevel, logrotate config persisted, all 7 rotated files intact, and a new write to app.log succeeded

evidence.requirement: logrotate installed and daily rotation configured for /var/log/inventory/app.log with 7 compressed rotations and continued-writability (copytruncate)
evidence.summary: logrotate package installed (ships /etc/periodic/daily/logrotate); /etc/logrotate.d/inventory written with daily/rotate 7/compress/delaycompress/copytruncate; dry-run confirms config parses and targets app.log with 7 rotations

evidence.requirement: cron mechanism enabled so rotation actually runs daily (not just configured)
evidence.summary: crond was found stopped/not enabled; added to default runlevel and started, confirmed status started

evidence.requirement: Rotation behavior works end-to-end: rotates, compresses, retains exactly 7, and app continues writing after rotation without interruption
evidence.summary: Forced rotation cycles show app.log truncated/copytruncate working (new writes succeed immediately post-rotation), delaycompress leaves newest rotation uncompressed then compresses on next cycle, and after 8 forced cycles exactly 7 rotated files (app.log.1 uncompressed + app.log.2.gz..7.gz) are retained, oldest discarded
Captured boot_id 2fe1aadd-df70-4843-9cae-ea9ceb0bc67e, crond started, logrotate config present, 7 rotated files present, and a live write appended successfully to app.log
Backgrounded 'sleep 2; reboot' command returned 'reboot scheduled' immediately, before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart proof via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Connection dropped/timed out during reboot, then exec succeeded again with boot_id 1df7ec97-f3fa-4f49-83ea-82fc62af764c (different from baseline 2fe1aadd...) and uptime -s showing fresh boot time 07:52:34, proving an actual restart

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services and data on node1
evidence.summary: After reboot: crond auto-started and enabled in default runlevel, /etc/logrotate.d/inventory config intact, all 7 previously rotated files still present, and a new write to app.log succeeded confirming the log remains writable
